screens.prompt: In B9, say missing when the code in A8 is not in the table, and found when it is.

hints.syntax: =IF(ISNA(MATCH(A8,A2:A7,0)),"missing","found"): the test sits inside the IF.
hints.func-if: Two words come out of the formula, so an IF has to choose between them.
hints.func-isna: MATCH raises #N/A when it fails, and ISNA recognises that error alone.
hints.require-ref: Search for the code held in A8 rather than typing Q-9.
hints.value: Q-9 is not in the code column, so the match fails and the IF prints missing, not found.
hints.error: Swapping the two words is the common mistake: with found in the true branch, a miss prints found.

reject.why: there is no match here, so nothing is tested and the code itself is returned
a comparison to the code can only answer for that one value, not for a lookup that misses
the two words are the wrong way round, so a miss reads as found
the code is typed into the match instead of read from the grid
the word missing is then divided by zero
the missing parenthesis breaks the nested call

screens.prompt: In B9, ask the table for a third column and say out of range when that column does not exist, otherwise fine.

hints.syntax: =IF(ISERROR(INDEX(A2:B7,1,3)),"out of range","fine"): the test wraps the whole call.
hints.func-if: The answer is one of two words, so the test goes inside an IF.
hints.func-iserror: ISNA would answer fine here, because a #REF! is not #N/A.
hints.require-ref: Point at A2:B7 itself rather than at a range you type out.
hints.value: A two-column table has no third column, so INDEX fails and the answer is out of range.
hints.error: The test on its own returns TRUE or FALSE. The grader wants the word out of range.

reject.why: a #REF! is not #N/A, so the narrower test answers fine
the second column exists, so nothing fails and the answer is fine
the two words are the wrong way round, so a real #REF! reads as fine
the test alone returns true or false, and the question asks for a word
a different range is tested, so the grid's table is never read
the text answer is then divided by zero
the IF is missing its opening parenthesis

docs.explain:
An error in Excel is a value sitting in a cell, so a formula can test it like a number. ISNA answers TRUE only for #N/A, the error a lookup or a match raises when nothing matched. ISERROR answers TRUE for any error at all. ISERR is the same test with #N/A taken out.

The first screen asks about Q-9, which the code column does not hold, so MATCH fails and ISNA prints missing. The second asks INDEX for a third column of A2:B7, and the table has two, so the call fails with #REF! and ISERROR prints out of range.

The three errors differ in kind. #N/A is a data question: the list does not hold the code. #REF! is a formula question: the range does not reach that far. #VALUE! is arithmetic handed text where it expected a number.

errors.text: Nothing matched: the code in A8 is not in the list MATCH searched.
The reference lies outside the range, as a column number past the last column does.
Arithmetic was handed text, as dividing the word missing by zero does.

docs.atWork: An import log that says which rows have no matching product code, so nobody scrolls a column of #N/A.
docs.outcome: Tell a missing match apart from a broken reference, and print that difference as words.
docs.teaches: ISNA versus ISERROR, and how #N/A, #REF! and #VALUE! are produced
docs.dataset: Code and price table with one code the table does not hold

seo.title: Read #N/A, #VALUE! and #REF! in Excel
seo.description: #N/A means a value is not in the list, #REF! a reference points at nothing, #VALUE! the wrong type met arithmetic. ISNA and ISERROR tell them apart.
